title: POC Sprint Charter - BlueWave kickoff
content:
POC Sprint Charter — BlueWave: Private inference for PHI-aware document search

Objective:
- Deliver a working private deployment (VPC) of Redwood that powers semantic search over BlueWave patient documents (PHI scope), with an initial UI and an API proxy for their EHR pipeline.
- Validate latency, relevance, security controls, and operator runbooks so BlueWave can decide on Dedicated vs Private licensing.

Primary success criteria (measurable):
- Relevance: embedding-retrieval recall@10 >= 0.85 on the BlueWave holdout set (200 queries)
- Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end query latency <= 300ms for short queries (<=64 tokens) under target load (50 QPS)
- Throughput/scale: sustain 50 QPS with <=10% CPU/GPU queuing and average token generation time per token <= 7ms
- Cost signal: projected monthly token+infra cost <= $X (placeholder, will model after infra sizing)
- Security/compliance: pass BlueWave security checklist items 1–8 (network isolation, KMS-managed keys, audit logs, no PHI egress) and sign-off from BlueWave security team
- Operational: documented runbook with rollback and fallback to hosted Redwood model variant; 1-hour recovery time objective (RTO) for common failures

Qualitative acceptance:
- BlueWave product PM signs off that search results are 'useful' in a 1-hour interactive session
- SE demo shows how to reproduce a regression with a prompt set and target metrics

Scope and out-of-scope:
- In-scope: private control plane + VPC peering, model onboarding (curated retrieval model + embedding model), optimizer config (caching/batching), small UI for search, E2E metrics instrumentation
- Out-of-scope: full EHR integration, multi-tenant aggregation, long-term retention policy design (will be follow-on)

Team & roles:
- SE lead: Maya Chen (owner) — technical owner, infra coordination, customer workshops
- Solution engineer: Jordan Lee — model config, eval harness, embeddings
- Infra SRE: Samir Gupta — VPC, KMS, network, capacity config
- Product PM (BlueWave liaison): Priya Natarajan — success criteria, acceptance
- Security reviewer: Claire Thompson — security checklist, threat model
- Customer contacts: Dr. Elena Morales (BlueWave PM), Aaron Cho (BlueWave SecOps)

Kickoff workshop agenda (90 min):
- 0–10min: intros, goals
- 10–25min: BlueWave requirements and redlines (security, latency, data residency)
- 25–45min: Proposed architecture walk-through (VPC, control plane, model variants, routing/fallback)
- 45–60min: Data and access checklist (sample docs, de-identification, ingest pipeline)
- 60–75min: Success criteria and evaluation plan (metrics, holdout, queries)
- 75–90min: Next steps, action items, timeline

Prereqs for workshop / POC kickoff:
- BlueWave to grant test dataset (sftp or cloud bucket) with sample consent and schema by D+5
- Security questionnaire completed (initial) by D+3
- Access: a BlueWave engineer with VPC/network admin rights on the call
- Jira POC ticket created (POC-482) and Confluence spec linked

Data & privacy notes (working):
- Default plan: customer-managed bucket in same region + VPC peering; artifacts remain in BlueWave account
- Hold an in-person security review if customer insists on HSM-backed keying
- Unresolved: need clarification if PHI can be used to finetune on-host models; assume no until legal confirms

Eval plan (short):
- Curate 200 query holdout with 10 relevance judgments each
- Run batch eval with embeddings + ANN (nprobe) and reranking model; capture recall@k, MRR, P95 latency
- Run load test simulating 50 QPS (gradual ramp) with representative token distributions

Milestones & timeline (8-week sprint):
- Week 0: Kickoff + security questionnaire
- Week 1–2: Infra setup (VPC peering, KMS, RBAC), deploy control plane
- Week 3: Model onboarding + smoke tests (local eval)
- Week 4: Integrate with BlueWave sample data, run first relevance eval
- Week 5: Load testing + tuning (batching, cache params)
- Week 6: Workshop: review results, iterate on configs
- Week 7: Final demo + handover doc and runbook
- Week 8: Acceptance window + signoff

Risks & mitigations (notes):
- Risk: Customer dataset requires heavy de-identification -> Mitigation: propose synthetic subset for early evals
- Risk: Network approvals delay VPC peering -> Mitigation: run a hosted sandbox with strict data scrubbing until peering completes
- Risk: Model quality gap -> Mitigation: run A/B with alternative quantized model, adjust reranker

Deliverables (what we'll hand over):
- Infra diagram + URLs for control plane and admin console
- Evaluation report with recall/latency curves and prompt set
- Runbook: incident steps, rollback, fallback to hosted API
- Cost estimate and recommended Dedicated vs Private plan

Open questions / action items (triaged):
- [Maya] Confirm billing target $X threshold for cost acceptance (D+2)
- [Jordan] Prepare initial 200-query holdout (D+4)
- [Samir] Share VPC peering checklist and required BlueWave CIDR ranges (D+3)
- [Claire] Schedule security review call with BlueWave SecOps (D+5)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the first demo as simple as possible — search UI + explainability snippet
- Collect top-10 failure cases in the first week
- Consider running small quantized model for initial latency wins

Sign-off (acceptance):
- Acceptance will be a 2-party sign-off: BlueWave PM + Redwood SE lead
- Document final metrics snapshot and attach to Jira POC ticket

References:
- Confluence: BlueWave POC spec (linked above)
- Jira: POC-482
- Template: se-poc-kickoff-template
